Record date: 2129-10-10
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 10/10/29 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Improved respiratory symptoms but persistent fatigue and increased sputum production.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for a follow-up visit one week after his last appointment. He reports a noticeable improvement in his respiratory symptoms since the initiation of the short course of oral prednisone and the adjustment of his nebulized albuterol regimen. The frequency of wheezing has decreased, and he is now using the nebulizer every hour as needed, finding it more effective than before. However, he continues to experience increased sputum production, which remains clear, and he notes persistent fatigue that has not significantly improved.
Despite the improvement in wheezing, Mr. Fairfax expresses concern regarding his ongoing fatigue, which he attributes to both his COPD and his underlying congestive heart failure. He denies any episodes of chest pain, orthopnea, or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea since the last visit. He has also been compliant with his furosemide regimen and has not noticed any swelling in his legs.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + persistent fatigue, - weight loss, - fever, - chills, - night sweats. Pulmonary - + decreased wheezing, + persistent cough with clear sputum, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain, - orthopnea, - paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - no joint pain. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: - Blood Pressure: 130/76 mmHg - Heart Rate: 80 bpm - Respiratory Rate: 20 breaths/min - Oxygen Saturation: 90% on room air.
General: The patient appears moderately fatigued but is alert and in no acute distress.
HEENT: No nasal flaring; oropharynx clear, no signs of dehydration.
Lungs: Mild wheezing noted on auscultation, particularly on forced expiration; prolonged expiration present, but no crackles.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs or gallops; peripheral pulses intact and symmetric.
Extremities: No edema; no tenderness on palpation.
ASSESSMENT
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) improving; persistent cough with clear sputum and mild wheezing likely indicating ongoing airway inflammation. 2. Congestive heart failure stable; no signs of fluid overload. 3. Persistent fatigue likely multifactorial, related to COPD exacerbation and underlying cardiac condition.
PLAN
1. Continue nebulized albuterol every hour as needed; consider transitioning to a long-acting beta-agonist (LABA) in conjunction with a LAMA for improved long-term management. 2. Taper oral prednisone to 20 mg daily for 5 days, then discontinue; monitor for any resurgence of symptoms. 3. Continue oral furosemide 40 mg daily; reassess fluid status and renal function at the next visit. 4. Schedule follow-up in two weeks for further evaluation of respiratory symptoms, fatigue, and overall health status. 5. Encourage patient to engage in light physical activity as tolerated to combat fatigue and improve overall endurance.
Mr. Fairfax was advised to maintain a symptom diary, noting any changes in sputum production, wheezing, or fatigue levels, and to seek medical attention promptly if his symptoms worsen.
DISPOSITION
Mr. Fairfax was discharged home with updated medication instructions, including the tapering schedule for prednisone and continued use of nebulized albuterol. A follow-up appointment has been scheduled for two weeks from today to monitor progress and adjust the treatment plan as necessary.
